entries.label: RBC Newcomer Advantage credit-card limit (advertised maximum)
entries.notes: For PRs/international students arrived within 12 months, or temporary foreign workers within 48 months. No Canadian credit history required; eligibility and credit criteria still apply.
entries.source_note: RBC press release (Sept 2026) + rbcroyalbank.com Newcomer Advantage terms, read 2026-10-01.

entries.label: Scotiabank StartRight newcomer card limit (advertised maximum)
entries.notes: No Canadian credit history required. One Scotiabank landing-page variant shows 'up to $5,000' in the same footnote position; the StartRight pages and newcomer rewards guide cite up to $15,000. Prefer the StartRight-page figure.

entries.label: BMO NewStart unsecured newcomer card limit (advertised maximum)
entries.notes: No credit history required; if unsecured is declined, a secured card with deposit is still available. Apply in branch with immigration document + photo ID.
entries.source_note: BMO 'Credit Cards for Newcomers' page, read 2026-10-01.

entries.label: CIBC newcomer first-card annual fee rebate period
entries.notes: First Canadian credit card with no credit history required.
entries.source_note: CIBC Welcome to Canada official form page, read 2026-10-01.

entries.source_note: CIBC Welcome to Canada official form page, read 2026-10-01.

entries.notes: Supersedes older $59-fee versions of this card still shown on some aggregator pages.

entries.label: Capital One Guaranteed Secured purchase APR
entries.notes: Same rate applies to balance transfers and cash advances.

entries.label: Capital One Guaranteed Secured minimum security deposit
entries.notes: Official page only says 'security funds may be required' without a dollar range. money.ca (Apr 2026): $75-$300; finder.com: minimum $75, limit cap $2,500.

entries.label: Neo Secured Mastercard minimum deposit
entries.notes: Lowest secured-card deposit minimum in the Canadian market.
entries.source_note: Neo Financial official blog (current page), read 2026-10-01.

entries.label: Neo Build membership monthly fee
entries.notes: Conflicts with the official disclosure statement, which lists a $5/month Secured Card Fee 'excluding customers on Build and Grow memberships' - the base-vs-bundle structure is ambiguous on Neo's own pages. Confirm at application.

entries.label: Neo secured-card base-plan fee (per disclosure statement)
entries.notes: Disclosure Statement and Fee Schedule (2026-04-15): 'Secured Card Fee: $5 monthly fee (excluding customers on Build and Grow memberships)'. Conflicts with the $9.99/month Build-membership figure on Neo's blog; treat the fee structure as ambiguous until Neo clarifies.

entries.label: Home Trust Secured Visa minimum deposit
entries.notes: Two pricing options: $0 annual fee at 19.99% purchases, or $59 annual fee at 14.90% purchases. Not available in Quebec. Reports to both bureaus.
entries.source_note: finvyu.com fees page (states rates checked 2026-09-22 against Home Trust official site), read 2026-10-01.

entries.label: Home Trust Secured Visa fee/rate options
entries.notes: Same secondary sourcing caveat as newcomer.hometrust_min_deposit.
entries.source_note: finvyu.com fees page (rates checked 2026-09-22 vs official site), read 2026-10-01.

entries.label: Triangle Mastercard published minimum credit score
entries.notes: Claim appears on content-farm-style pages (financeply/medifacto) quoting Triangle terms; not verified on triangle.canadiantire.ca this session. SIN listed as optional on the application.
entries.value: no published minimum on eligibility page

entries.label: Prepaid cards do not build credit in Canada
entries.notes: FCAC: 'Beware of prepaid products that claim they will improve your credit rating. This is false advertising.' KOHO Credit Building subscription ($7-$10/mo) reports a small tradeline to Equifax but is not a revolving credit card.
entries.source_note: FCAC publication (archived) + rates.ca secured-vs-prepaid guide, read 2026-10-01.

entries.label: SIN is required to apply for credit products in Canada
entries.notes: SIN is a 9-digit identifier; newcomers (PR, work/study permit holders) can apply at Service Canada on arrival. Bureaus also use it for identity matching.

entries.label: Time to first Canadian credit score for newcomers
entries.notes: First score typically lands in the fair range (560-659). A 'good' score (660+) typically takes 1-2 years of steady behaviour (Wealthsimple Learn).

entries.label: Worked example: $500 balance carried 12 months at 29.9%
entries.notes: Python-verified 2026-10-01: 500*(1+0.299/12)^12 - 500. Used in the explainer's Traps section.

entries.label: Worked example: $200 cash advance held 60 days at 29.9%
entries.notes: Python-verified 2026-10-01: 200*(1+0.299/365)^60 - 200, before cash-advance fees. Used in the explainer's Traps section.

entries.label: Worked example: $60 on a $500 limit = 12% utilization
entries.notes: Python-verified 2026-10-01. Under-30% guidance from FCAC; under-10% ideal. $450 on $500 = 90% counter-case.
